meta.titre: Communication Services: matching post, courier and phone to the need
meta.sous_theme: Postal services, courier, telecommunications and postage calculations

sections.contenu_markdown: A student abroad needs to send a certificate to a university, a company wants to send a signed contract and be able to prove it was sent, and a tourist in a town wants to receive letters although she has no address there. Each of them needs a different communication service. The GCE Commerce papers ask you to define the postal services, to choose the right one for a situation and to explain what each service offers. This course gives you the services and a method for choosing between them.

items: Aids to trade are services such as communication, banking, transport, insurance and warehousing that help trade to take place.
A letter or parcel needs an address and payment of postage.
Information can be sent in writing, by voice or in electronic form.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Why communication matters in trade

Buyers and sellers must exchange orders, quotations, invoices, payments and complaints. Fast and reliable communication saves time and avoids misunderstanding.

### Postal services

| Service | What it offers |
|---|---|
| Ordinary mail | Letters and cards delivered for the normal postage; cheap, but with no proof of posting and no special care |
| Registered post | An extra fee buys a receipt as proof of posting, careful handling and a signature on delivery; compensation may be paid if the item is lost; used for valuable or important documents |
| Express mail or courier | Faster delivery, often with tracking, for a higher fee |
| Parcel post | Carries parcels; the charge depends on weight (and often distance) |
| Post restante | Mail is addressed to a post office and kept there until the person collects it, usually after showing identification; useful for travellers, tourists and people with no fixed address |
| Post office box | A numbered box rented from the post office, from which a customer collects mail |
| Money order | A safe way to send a sum of money by post: the sender pays the amount and a fee, and the receiver cashes it at a post office |

A **franking machine** is used by firms with a lot of mail. It prints the postage on each item instead of stamps, and its meter records the amount used, which saves time and avoids lost stamps.

### Telecommunication services

The **telephone** (fixed and mobile) gives immediate two-way voice contact. **E-mail** and the **internet** carry messages, documents and pictures in seconds and keep a written record. Mobile phone services also allow money to be sent and payments to be made.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a situation is described and you must recommend a service
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask four questions: how **fast** must it arrive, how **much** can be spent, is **proof** needed, and how **valuable** is the item? Proof of posting points to registered post, speed to express mail or e-mail, a traveller with no address to post restante, a large daily volume of mail to a franking machine.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'briefly explain' a service
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a definition in your own words, then one fact about how it works or who uses it. For example: 'Money order: a way of sending money by post. The sender pays the amount plus a fee and the receiver cashes it at a post office.' Do not just repeat the name of the service.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When tariffs are given and you must cost a batch of mail
variantes.contenu_markdown: Cost of a registered item $= \text{postage} + \text{registration fee}$. For parcels, follow the tariff exactly, for example a first-weight charge plus a charge for each extra block of weight. Multiply by the number of items, then add all the totals.

sections.enonce_markdown: A firm uses the following hypothetical tariff. Ordinary letter: 300 FCFA. Registration fee for a registered letter: 800 FCFA extra. Parcel: 2,000 FCFA for the first kilogram and 600 FCFA for each additional kilogram. The firm sends 40 ordinary letters, 6 registered letters and 2 parcels of 3 kg each. (a) Calculate the total cost. (b) Explain why the firm registers the 6 letters.

etapes.justification: Number of letters times the postage.
Each registered letter pays the postage plus the registration fee.
First kilogram at 2,000 FCFA, then 2 additional kilograms at 600 FCFA each.
Two parcels of the same weight.
The total is the sum of the three items.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **The total cost is 25,000 FCFA.** The firm registers the 6 letters because registered post gives a receipt as proof of posting, careful handling, a signature on delivery and possible compensation if the letters are lost. These are useful for important or valuable documents.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Registered post is the fastest way to send a letter.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Registration gives proof of posting, extra care and a signature on delivery. It does not make delivery faster.
items.correction_markdown: Registered post offers security and proof; express mail offers speed.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Post restante means the mail is delivered to the addressee's house.'
items.pourquoi_faux: In post restante the mail is kept at a post office and the addressee collects it there.
items.correction_markdown: Post restante: mail held at a named post office for collection, useful for travellers and tourists.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A franking machine is a machine used by the post office to sort mail.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A franking machine is owned by a firm and prints postage on its mail in place of stamps.
items.correction_markdown: A franking machine prints the postage on mail and records the amount used; it is used by businesses.

items.erreur_markdown: Answering 'briefly explain registered post' with 'Registered post is mail that is registered.'
items.pourquoi_faux: This repeats the term and says nothing about what the service offers.
items.correction_markdown: Registered post is a service where, for an extra fee, the sender gets a receipt as proof of posting and the item is handled with extra care and signed for on delivery.

items.erreur_markdown: Recommending ordinary mail for a valuable document
items.pourquoi_faux: Ordinary mail gives no proof of posting and no compensation if the item is lost.
items.correction_markdown: Use registered post, or a courier with tracking, for valuable or important documents.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the most suitable service: (a) a tourist staying a few days in a town without an address there who wants to receive letters; (b) a firm that must prove it posted an important document; (c) a company that posts hundreds of letters a day and wants to avoid sticking stamps on each.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Post restante**. (b) **Registered post**, since it gives a receipt as proof of posting. (c) **A franking machine**, which prints postage on the letters.

items.enonce_markdown: Under a hypothetical tariff, an ordinary letter costs 250 FCFA and registration costs 700 FCFA extra per letter. A firm posts 30 ordinary letters and 8 registered letters. Calculate the total postage.
items.solution_markdown:
Ordinary letters: $30 \times 250 = 7\,500$ FCFA.

Registered letters: $8 \times (250 + 700) = 8 \times 950 = 7\,600$ FCFA.

Total $= 7\,500 + 7\,600 = 15\,100$ FCFA.

**Total postage: 15,100 FCFA.**

items.enonce_markdown: A supplier must send a signed agreement to a customer in another country. (a) Give two advantages and one limitation of sending it by registered post. (b) Give two advantages of sending a scanned copy by e-mail. (c) Under a hypothetical tariff, a parcel costs 1,200 FCFA for the first 500 g and 400 FCFA for each additional 500 g or part of it. Calculate the cost of a parcel weighing 2.3 kg.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Advantages (any two): a receipt proves posting; the original signed paper arrives; delivery is signed for; compensation may be paid if it is lost. Limitation (any one): it is slower than e-mail; it costs more than ordinary mail.

(b) Any two: it arrives in seconds; it costs little; it leaves a written record; it can be sent at any hour.

(c) 2.3 kg is 2,300 g, which is 5 blocks of 500 g (the last one only part full). The first block costs 1,200 FCFA and the other 4 blocks cost $4 \times 400 = 1\,600$ FCFA. Total $= 1\,200 + 1\,600 = 2\,800$ FCFA.

**Parcel cost: 2,800 FCFA.**

items_markdown: Ordinary mail is the cheapest postal service but gives no proof of posting; registered post adds a receipt, extra care and a signature on delivery.
Express mail or courier gives faster delivery, often with tracking, for a higher fee.
Post restante keeps mail at a post office for collection, which suits tourists and travellers with no address in the town.
A franking machine, used by businesses, prints postage on mail in place of stamps and records the amount used.
Telephone, e-mail and the internet give fast contact and, for e-mail, a written record.
To choose a service, ask about speed, cost, proof and the value of the item.
